name: SMART-1
short_status: Impacted the Moon Sep 3, 2006: last signal 05:42:22 UT from Lacus Excellentiae; the infrared flash was recorded from Hawaii, and LRO images located the 4 by 20 m impact gouge in 2017.

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 27 September 2003, 23:14 UT, Ariane 5 Flight 162 from Kourou, French Guiana, riding as an auxiliary passenger with two commercial telecom satellites into a 742 x 36,016 km transfer orbit

facts.label: Spacecraft
facts.value: 367 kg at launch, including a 19 kg science payload; about 14 m across with solar arrays deployed

facts.label: Propulsion
facts.value: Snecma PPS-1350 Hall-effect ion engine: 0.07 N of thrust from up to 1,350 W of solar power, fed by 82 kg of xenon

facts.label: Propulsion firsts
facts.value: By ESA's count, the second mission ever to use ion propulsion as its primary propulsion system, after NASA's Deep Space 1 (launched October 1998); Japan's Hayabusa, launched May 2003, was also already flying ion main propulsion. Unambiguously the first European spacecraft to travel to and orbit the Moon

facts.label: Lunar capture
facts.value: 15 November 2004, during a five-day braking thrust, after a cruise of about 13 months from geostationary transfer orbit

facts.label: Ion engine totals
facts.value: 4,958.3 hours of thruster operation across the mission; final firing 17 September 2005, with the xenon effectively exhausted

facts.label: Science orbit
facts.value: Polar ellipse from roughly 300 to 3,000 km altitude, pericentre between 300 and 450 km near the Moon's south pole

facts.label: Instruments
facts.value: AMIE miniaturized camera, D-CIXS X-ray spectrometer, SIR infrared spectrometer and the XSM X-ray solar monitor, packed into a 19 kg payload

facts.label: Calcium first
facts.value: 15 January 2005: D-CIXS makes the first unambiguous remote-sensing detection of calcium on the Moon, over Mare Crisium, using a solar flare as its X-ray source

facts.label: Mission cost
facts.value: 110 million euros total, including the launch, operations and a dozen experiments; developed in under four years

facts.label: Impact
facts.value: 3 September 2006: last signal at 05:42:22 UT via ESA's New Norcia station; impact at about 2 km/s on a roughly 1-degree grazing trajectory at 34.4 S, 46.2 W in Lacus Excellentiae (Lake of Excellence)

facts.label: Flash observed from Earth
facts.value: The 3.6 m Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope on Mauna Kea recorded the infrared impact flash at 2.12 microns and a debris cloud travelling some 80 km in about 130 seconds; the impact came on lunar orbit 2,890

timeline: Launch at 23:14 UT as an auxiliary passenger on Ariane 5 Flight 162 from Kourou, into a 742 x 36,016 km geostationary transfer orbit
The PPS-1350 ion engine fires in space for the first time, on the fourth orbit; months of perigee thrust arcs follow, the longest 56.7 hours
Lunar capture during a five-day braking thrust: the first time electric propulsion carries a spacecraft to capture by the gravity of another celestial body
During a solar flare, D-CIXS makes the first unambiguous remote-sensing detection of calcium on the Moon, over Mare Crisium
Spiral-down complete: SMART-1 settles into its operational polar science orbit (science observations had already begun in January during the descent)
Final ion engine firing, closing the books at 4,958.3 hours of thruster operation with the xenon effectively spent

With the xenon gone, a two-week series of manoeuvres on the small hydrazine attitude thrusters steers the inevitable impact away from an unobserved far-side end (due August 17) to the near side, in view of Earth-based telescopes; provision is made for minor trims in late July, August and early September
Impact in Lacus Excellentiae on lunar orbit 2,890; New Norcia loses the signal at 05:42:22 UT, and CFHT in Hawaii records the infrared flash and debris cloud

The impact scar is identified in Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter camera images: a 4 m wide, 20 m long gouge at 34.262 S, 46.193 W (identification credited P. Stooke/B. Foing et al. 2017; Stooke's analysis published in Icarus, 2019)
